catalog_quote: Phonological words in Rục can be either monosyllabic or sesquisyllabic. Sesquisyllabic words are characteristic of many Austroasiatic languages (Thomas, 1992) and consist of two parts: a main stressed syllable exhibiting the full phonemic inventory and an unstressed presyllable that has a more restricted phonemic structure and is subject to reduction. Presyllables are highly variable between speakers. The segmental structures of mono- and sesqui-syllables are as follows: Monosyllabic: C1 (C2) V (C3) / T; Sesquisyllabic: (Cp1) v (Cp2).C1 (C2) V (C3) / T where C1 is the consonant onset of the main syllable, C2 is one of the liquids or semivowels /l, r, w/, V is the obligatory main vowel (monophthong or diphthong), C3 is the coda (a consonant or a glide), Cp1 is the onset of the presyllable, v is the vowel of the presyllable, Cp2 is the coda of the presyllable, and T is the tone of the mai…

new_statements.rule_in_words: Rục (Chut) words are monosyllables or sesquisyllables (presyllable + main syllable). Stress falls on the main syllable, i.e. the last syllable of the word; the preceding presyllable is unstressed, segmentally restricted, reducible and tonally neutral. The main syllable also carries the four-way tone/register contrast (A1, A2, B1, B2), so the language is tonal with iambic word stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned (words are at most presyllable + main syllable).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; presyllables are 'highly variable between speakers' and 'subject to reduction'.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word (citation forms and wordlist elicitation, 20 speakers of the Rục dialect at Mò O Ồ Ồ, Thượng Hóa commune, Minh Hóa district, Quảng Bình; field trips 2019 and 2021). The statement is framed as the standard Austroasiatic sesquisyllable definition applied to Rục; no acoustic evidence for stress is given (the dissertation's instrumental work concerns tone/register on the main syllable). Tạ (p. 117) states Rục, Mày and Sách are mutually intelligible with the same tonation system, but the stress statement is made for Rục only.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes the Rục dialect (Glottolog rucc1239, a dialect of Chut chut1247), from the author's own 2019/2021 fieldwork at Mò O Ồ Ồ, Thượng Hóa, Minh Hóa, Quảng Bình. The most authoritative description of Chut, Babaev & Samarina 2021, describes the Mày dialect (mayy1239) and was not accessible. The Badosa Roldós 2025 thesis quoted in sources_examined (stress on the main/second element, iambic) is for Malieng (mali1278 under Maleng male1282 in Glottolog) — ISO 639-3 [scb] folds Mã Liềng into Chut, but Glottolog does not, so it is recorded only as a comparison, not as the chut1247 statement.

sources.note: §5.1.2.1 Phonological word, p. 184: Rục words are monosyllabic or sesquisyllabic; a sesquisyllable consists of 'a main stressed syllable exhibiting the full phonemic inventory and an unstressed presyllable' subject to reduction. Also p. 126 (Proto-Vietic word = unstressed presyllable + stressed main syllable) and pp. 130-131 (Proto-Vietic's only suprasegmental = 'the iambic stress of the sesquisyllabic structure'). Based on the author's own field recordings of 20 Rục speakers (Mò O Ồ Ồ, Thượng Hóa, Minh Hóa, Quảng Bình), 2019 and 2021.
